decisions.reason: As a component closely tied to the established radiant-heater business, it likely benefits from the firm's growth and slack, but its lower prominence suggests it would be easier to discontinue than the strategic headline products.

Management is likely to retain this flagship electric line because it fits the firm's strategic move toward lower-carbon integrated climate solutions and the expanding firm can afford to support it while results mature.

This product is related to the core offer and can be carried by current organisational slack, but its more limited strategic emphasis makes it more vulnerable if early market results fall short of aspirations.

A multi-model industrial electric hall-heater line is close to the firm's core customer needs and direction, so a growing firm with broad capabilities would likely continue it unless performance clearly disappointed.
This hydrogen-capable flagship line is strongly aligned with the firm's stated future direction and already had a real operating installation, making management very likely to keep backing it.
